facts.subject: (unnamed) kindred of the Bull
facts.statement: The mountain folk count all passers-by as foes except kin and known friends.

refs.q: And are all men your foemen who pass through these mountains?

facts.subject: (unnamed) kindred of the Bull
facts.statement: Bull values lineage and despises kinless chapmen and their hired swordsmen.

refs.q: they know not the name of their mother's mother, nor have heard one word of the beginner of their kindred

facts.subject: Bull Shockhead
facts.statement: He says a bought thrall's life is not so bad; some have thralls of their own under them.

refs.q: this life of a bought thrall is not such an exceeding evil life

facts.subject: (unnamed) Maiden of Bourton Abbas
facts.statement: Captured, she showed no weeping but patience and intent to endure.

refs.q: there was no weeping or screeching in her, but patience rather and quietness, and intent to bear all and live

events.label: Ralph learns of the captor
events.summary: Bull tells Ralph his kinsman Bull Nosy took the maiden to Cheaping Knowe.

refs.q: But, lord, I will do my best to find her for thee

unresolved.question: Whether "Bull" names a whole kindred (later the merchant says men of that folk are so named).

opportunities.idea: Clan-based naming conventions (kindred name plus nickname) for a mountain culture's NPC names.

ledger.summary: Riding on, Bull Shockhead, now cheerful, defends his people's man-stealing as no worse than creditors and manor lords, and says thralls are often treated softly. He begs not to be sold. He says his kinsman Bull Nosy recently took a fair, strong, patient woman with a necklace like Ralph's and took her to market at Cheaping Knowe. Ralph says he would ransom her, and Bull promises to help find her.
ledger.geography_notes: Bull Nosy took his captive down to the market at Cheaping Knowe.
open_questions: Are the mountain people's names (Bull Shockhead, Bull Nosy) a kindred naming system?
